readMe: Revenue error = ln(actual/forecast); bias > 0 means the model forecast too LOW. Margin errors are in margin points (0.02 = 2 pts).
skill = 1 - model median abs error / baseline median abs error. Positive = the model beats that naive forecast; negative = the naive forecast was more accurate.
Baselines: fade = trailing 3-yr revenue CAGR fading to 4% by year 5; trend = trailing CAGR held; flat = no growth; median3 / last = margin persists.
Historical runs have no analyst estimates, so consensus-based rules are not tested here (see forecast-accuracy.json for live tracking).
Group tables (by growth, sector, category, reliability, flag, snapshot year) use the year 3 horizon.
headline: year 1: revenue off by a median 6.1% (bias -0.9%, 30% better than the naive fade); net margin off by 3.1 pts (bias 0.2 pts, 16% better than "3-yr median margin persists")

marginTrendTest.readMe: Forecasts where the rule fired, scored with and without it against what the companies reported. Lower medianAbsError and ruleCloserRate > 0.5 = the rule helps. Bias > 0 = forecast too LOW.

fcfVariantTest.readMe: Error = actual FCF margin - forecast, in margin points. skillVsModel > 0 = the variant was more accurate than the model. Decision rule (set in advance): adopt a variant only if it beats the model by 3%+ at years 3 and 5, is closer more than half the time at both, and wins in both halves of the snapshot dates at year 3.

variants.glide: last FCF margin -> 3-yr median by year 3
variants.conv: model net margin x trailing FCF/net income

byRank.note: Live rank at the snapshot (owner rule). Negative bias = model too optimistic.
